title: Debug Capsule playbook: trace replay & telemetry sandbox
body:
Purpose:
This note defines the Debug Capsule pattern: an intentionally small, privacy-safe telemetry capture and replay sandbox that teams can create on-demand to reproduce, debug, and iterate on inference regressions and operational surprises. The capsule bundles minimal traces, metric slices, request payloads (sanitized), and a defined runbook so engineers can reproduce incidents locally or in an ephemeral cluster without pulling full production traces or broad-scale dashboards.

Why we need a capsule:
- Large multi-tenant traces are noisy and expensive to store/query. Capsules create compact, focused captures tied to a reproducible key.
- Enables safe sharing across teams (SRE, Serving, Model Ops, Solutions) without heavy PI/PHI exposure.
- Shortens time-to-debug by providing a standardized, machine-readable artifact that includes the exact telemetry and commands required to re-run a problematic workload.

When to create a Debug Capsule (decision guide):
- P99 latency spike with unclear root cause after initial triage (metric aggregates + single-request logs insufficient).
- Regressions after model rollout where samples show mismatched outputs but infra looked healthy.
- Intermittent failure modes where full traces would be >10MB or scatter across services.
- Post-mortem requests where a reproducible artifact is required for follow-up testing.

Capsule contents (fixed schema):
- capsule_id: reproducible key (example: dbg-20241009-<short-hash>)
- capture_window: start/end timestamps (UTC)
- tenant_scope: list of tenant tags included (or "single-tenant")
- sanitized_requests: up to N request payloads with PII removal rules applied (default N=25)
- trace_events: condensed spans for the target requests (no raw user data)
- metric_slices: time-series for key metrics (latency, error_count, retry_count, kv-cache-hits, batch-size) at 1s granularity for capture_window
- environment_snapshot: model_version, runtime_kernels, instance_type, quantization_profile, config_flags
- replay_instructions: CLI commands, container image tags, dataset pointers (if applicable)
- retention_ttl: how long the capsule will be stored (default 14 days)

Capture procedure (operator steps):
1) Open incident ticket and declare capsule intent: add tag "create-debug-capsule" to incident.
2) Select 1–3 representative request ids (via request-id header) from the incident window. If none, use top failure traces by latency.
3) Run capsule-capture tool with flags: --window <start,end> --requests <id,...> --sanitization-profile=standard. Tool outputs a zipped capsule and a capsule_id.
4) Upload artifact to capsule store (ephemeral object store with ACLs) and link to the incident ticket. Set retention TTL and team ACLs.
5) Notify stakeholders (SRE, model owner, serving lead) and assign replay owner.

Sanitization rules (non-negotiable):
- Strip or deterministic-hash any user identifiers (emails, phone numbers, account ids).
- Remove free-text user content unless explicitly required and approved by data-privacy. For approvals, include a signed justification in the capsule metadata.
- Replace embeddings and long blobs with summaries (length and checksum).

Trace and metric reduction heuristics (to make capsules compact):
- Collapse low-value spans (e.g., library-internal spans below 2ms) and keep an aggregate entry instead.
- Keep full KV-cache events for the chosen requests but sample cache-pop and cache-miss sequences only.
- Encode traces as a compact protobuf or ndjson with span anchors for quick lookups.

Sampling policy and budgeting:
- Default: 1 capsule per incident unless a total incident budget is requested.
- Capsule-capture runs against a query budget (1000 trace-segments per week per org) to avoid runaway costs.
- Operators may request quota increases through a short form on the observability console; quota changes require an owner approval.

Replay sandbox recipes (examples):
- Local Docker replay (fast path): docker run --rm -e CAPSULE_ID=dbg-20241009-abc123 replayer:prod "./replay --capsule $CAPSULE_ID --requests 3 --mode dryrun"
- Ephemeral cluster (scalable): trigger k8s job using replayer image with resources pinned to a small node pool; use canary routing to send safe percentages back to serving for closed-loop tests.

Dashboard templates to attach to capsule artifact:
- Capsule-summary panel: single-row showing capsule_id, capture_window, retention_ttl, owner, status
- Request waterfall: compact visualizer for the chosen requests with span durations normalized to node type
- Metric sparkline grid: per-metric 1s-series small multiples for latency/error/throughput/batching across the window
- Diff panel: baseline vs capture_window delta for p50/p90/p99 and token-cost-per-request estimates

Runbook: triage flow using a capsule (quick sequence):
1) Confirm capsule reproduces the anomaly in dry-run mode (no external side-effects). If reproduces, proceed; if not, expand capture window or add more requests.
2) Run baseline comparisons (metric diff panel) to isolate whether regression is model-logic, batching, or infra.
3) If trace shows high queuing or KV-cache contention, escalate to infra with the capsule attached and highlight cache-miss histograms.
4) If model outputs differ but latency looks normal, mark as model-regression and attach capsule to model-eval job for domain-specific tests.
5) After fix validation, extend capsule retention to 90 days for post-mortem and delete only after acceptance.

Operational notes and constraints:
- Capsules are not a replacement for full observability; they are a targeted debug tool. Long-term SLI/SLO work should still use aggregated dashboards.
- Access control: capsules inherit the incident's ACL; cross-org sharing must be explicitly permitted.
- Privacy review required for any capsule containing non-sanitized user content.

Implementation roadmap (rough milestones):
- Q4 2024: build capsule-capture prototype + basic sanitization plugin + capsule store with TTL and ACLs.
- Q1 2025: dashboard templates and replay image; integrate with incident UI to create capsules from ticket.
- Q2 2025: quota controls, audit logging, and sandboxed cluster for safe replays.

Open questions (practical engineering decisions we should pick soon):
- Default retention TTL: 7 vs 14 vs 30 days? (security/cost tradeoffs)
- How many request payloads should be allowed by default (25 vs 50)?
- Which fields must be always hashed vs allowed in cleartext for debugging efficiency?

Appendix: quick commands and examples
- Capture: capsule-capture --window 2024-11-01T18:22Z,2024-11-01T18:27Z --requests rq_abc123,rq_def456 --profile standard
- List capsules: capsule-store list --owner marta.nguyen --active-only
- Replay dry-run local: ./replayer --capsule dbg-20241009-abc123 --mode dryrun --max-requests 3

Notes to reviewers:
- Looking for feedback on the sanitization profile, default TTL, and the quota-guard thresholds. Also want suggestions for minimal dashboard panels that are most helpful in first 90s of triage.
- If you have recurring cases where we needed different telemetry slices (e.g., kernel-level GPU metrics), add them to the linked_artifacts or reply in the ticket.

End of document.
